title: Dyson V15 Detect Cordless Vacuum - Repair & Troubleshooting Manual
warnings: Always remove the battery before disassembly.
Do not wash any electrical components or the motor.
Allow filters to dry completely (24 hours) before reinstalling.
Do not use compressed air on the laser diode module.
The battery contains lithium cells — do not puncture or expose to heat.
inspection_prompts_for_agent: Can you see the LCD screen on top of the body?
Is there any blockage visible in the clear bin?
What color is the light ring around the trigger?
Can you see the green laser light when the floor head is on?
Does the brush bar spin freely when you rotate it by hand?

external_anatomy.top: LCD performance screen showing suction power and dust count
external_anatomy.body: Main motor unit with cyclone assembly (gold/nickel)
external_anatomy.front: Clear dust bin with red release lever
external_anatomy.attachment: Laser Slim Fluffy cleaner head with green laser

disassembly_steps.action: Remove battery by pressing the release button and sliding down
Remove dust bin by pressing the red release button
Remove filter by turning counter-clockwise on top of cyclone
disassembly_steps.note: Wash under cold water only, dry 24h

disassembly_steps.action: Remove cleaner head by pressing the red clip and pulling
disassembly_steps.note: Check brush bar for tangled hair/debris

disassembly_steps.action: Access brush bar by turning the end cap with a coin
disassembly_steps.note: Pull brush bar out and clean

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check for blockages
troubleshooting_steps.action: Remove the wand and cleaner head. Look through the wand for blockages. Check the inlet at the body.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: Pulsing on/off usually means a blockage or full bin.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Clean the filter
troubleshooting_steps.action: Remove the filter from the top of the cyclone. Wash under cold running water until water runs clear. Let dry 24 hours.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: Filter light on LCD means filter needs cleaning. A wet filter will cause the vacuum to not work.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check brush bar
troubleshooting_steps.action: Remove the cleaner head. Use a coin to turn the end cap and pull out the brush bar. Remove tangled hair and debris.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: If brush bar doesn't spin, check for obstructions or worn drive belt.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check battery
troubleshooting_steps.action: Fully charge the battery (3.5 hours). If it still dies quickly, the battery may need replacement.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: Flashing red light = low battery. Solid red = fault. Blue LEDs show charge level.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Reset the machine
troubleshooting_steps.action: Remove battery for 30 seconds. Reattach. This can clear some electronic faults.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: Try this if the LCD shows error codes or the trigger is unresponsive.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check laser module
troubleshooting_steps.action: The green laser is in the cleaner head. If not illuminating, ensure the head is fully clicked in. Check for debris on the laser lens.
troubleshooting_steps.condition: Laser only activates in Auto mode on hard floors.

stop_conditions: Motor makes grinding noise even after clearing blockages
Battery won't hold any charge after full cycle
LCD displays persistent error code after reset
follow_up_questions: Is the vacuum pulsing on and off, or completely dead?
When did you last clean the filter?
Does the LCD screen show anything?
Which cleaning head are you using?
hidden_fasteners: Battery has a hidden latch that requires firm push before slide
Brush bar end cap requires coin — not a screw

common_failures.likely_cause: Blockage in wand or cleaner head, or bin full
common_failures.fix: Clear blockage, empty bin, clean filter

common_failures.likely_cause: Clogged filter or bin not seated properly
common_failures.fix: Wash filter (dry 24h), reseat bin until it clicks

common_failures.likely_cause: Battery degradation or always running on Max mode
common_failures.fix: Use Auto mode. If still short, replace battery pack.

common_failures.likely_cause: Hair/string wrapped around bar, or worn belt
common_failures.fix: Remove and clean brush bar. Check drive belt.

notes: The V15 Detect has a piezo sensor that counts dust particles displayed on the LCD. The green laser helps reveal fine dust on hard floors. Always use Auto mode for best battery life.
